title: Capture of the canonical transition table
statement: Let $S$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $D$ be a four-work-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite bit strings. There is a natural number $t \le 3|\alpha|+5+c.\mathrm{canonizerTime}(|\alpha|)$ such that, after $t$ steps of the capture machine formed from the prefix machine and the canonizer of $c$, started on the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$, its state is $D$’s initial state, its input-head position is $2|\alpha|+3$, the tape corresponding to the captured transition table stores the buffer encoding of the serialization of the machine decoded from $\alpha$, and its output is empty.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is a four-work-tape binary Turing machine
There exists a natural number $t$ with $t \le 3|\alpha|+5+c.\mathrm{canonizerTime}(|\alpha|)$
replaced:
Let $S$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $c$ be an effective machine-coding
scheme, let $D$ be a four-tape binary machine with initial state $q_0$, and let
$\alpha,x$ be bit strings. Starting the capture machine built from the composed
prefix-extraction and canonizer machine for $c$, with interpreter $D$, on the paired
input $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, there is a time $t\le 3|\alpha|+5+T_c(|\alpha|)$ at
which its state is the interpreter state $q_0$, its input head is at position
$2|\alpha|+3$, its captured table tape contains the buffer-tape encoding of the
canonical serialization of the machine decoded from $\alpha$, and its output is empty.
